thread:
Anna L: Heads-up — ran an overnight quant+export workflow moving Gemma-lite -> Qwen-compatible weights. On long contexts (~1.2k+ tokens) we see token aliasing where some tail tokens appear to map to sentinel/pad IDs. Looks like a mid-roll vocab wrap.
Mike R: Can you paste the smallest repro? logs / diff would help.
Anna L: Paste of the trimmed log snippet:
```
[2026-03-20 03:14:02] input_ids: [101, 2034, 9999, ..., 50213, 50214, 2]
[2026-03-20 03:14:02] converted_ids: [101, 2034, 9999, ..., 13, 14, 2]
[2026-03-20 03:14:02] kv-cache-key token_id=50213 -> mapped to 13 (wrap)
embedding_diff L2: 0.42 for token 50213 vs expected 13
```
Sasha G: That smells like a token-id modulo wrap during the conversion step (we've seen this when vocab_size isn't passed through to the rotary/table exporter). Did you use the default convert script or the new converter? any nonzero vocab_offset?
Anna L: default convert (huggingface -> qwen export) with our int4 quant pipeline. No explicit vocab_offset passed.
eval-bot: Automated eval: long-doc perplexity +12.8% (baseline Gemma-lite fp16), rouge/bleu stats show quality drift on summarization slices >1024 tokens. Link: https://ci.redwood/ev/6332
Eva C: I can repro on a local int4 run (orion pool). Looks deterministic: after a certain token id threshold the K/V keys are indexing into the wrong embedding row. Probably the exporter clamps but then downstream code assumes fold.
Joel P: Could be rotary/key-position encoding mismatch too — if head-dim ordering changed we might be indexing a different slot and seeing "wrong token behaviour" that looks like wrap. Worth checking both the vocab mapping and the rotary head layout.
Mike R: Quick triage: reproduce -> bisect exporter commit chain -> check tokenizer normalization path. If it's exporter, we can hotfix with explicit pass-through of vocab_size and disable modulo. If tokenizer, might need remapping table.
Anna L: I ran a small bisect: commit range 1f3b..7a9d — the exporter change that touched the binary packing of vocab indices is suspicious (it introduced a uint16 -> uint12 packing for space savings). I think the pack/unpack is where high token ids get truncated.
Sasha G: Ah yes — that packing was meant for smaller models but accidentally applied to Gemma->Qwen path. Proposed quick fix: revert packing for vocab indices or add explicit "vocab_bits" param inferred from src vocab_size.
Anna L: I opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/convert/pull/4523 — adds safe path and unit test for max token id > 50000. Also adds a converter flag `--preserve-token-ids`.
Eva C: Reproduced PR patch locally, int4 run no longer shows aliasing on 2k token doc. Regression tests pass.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy: staging/gemmaqwen-convert/2026-03-20-11:30 (6332110200) :thumbsup:
Mike R: Nice. Plan: keep canary for 24h on staging with eval set, then cut a patch release for convert tool. Joel, Sasha — can you add a short test in onboarding harness that includes high token ids + long ctx? make it part of pre-onboard checks.
Joel P: Will add a harness test (token id ceiling + rotary permutes) — PR coming.
Sasha G: Also adding a check in model-onboard pipeline to assert converter flags: if model.vocab_size > 32768 ensure pack mode disabled.
Anna L: Adding note to model runbook: Watch for sudden perf spikes on long docs; set fallback routing to non-quantized Gemma variant until convert patch is rolled out to production.
Mike R: Sounds good. Who's owning production roll? Anna/Eva?
Eva C: I'll take prod rollout after 24h canary. Will also run a quick sweep across active dedicated customers to ensure no drift.
Anna L: Marking follow-ups: 1) merge PR 4523, 2) onboard-test PR from Joel, 3) pipeline assert from Sasha, 4) prod roll by Eva. Logging as incident-ish: INF-2026-03-20-01
Mike R: Thanks — small action items, big impact. :raised_hands:
Eva C: I'll file a short postmortem note after rollout and link the failing eval artifacts.
Anna L: Closing status: canary looks stable so far, tests green. Leaving more details in PR and runbook.
Joel P: Taking the test ownership — will ping when ready.
Anna L: Thanks everyone.
